label: Middle of the original input (steps 3-6) in sequences that start with n
explanation: Fires only in the original-input phase (98% of mass), plus a little at the delimiter step, and never during copy. Activity is confined to absolute steps 3-7, peaking at t=4-5, which carry about 84% of mass. It is driven by the first original token being n (first_tok=n: 21x lift, 85% of mass). The strongest examples start with n n or n h/f; sequences beginning with two n tokens give the highest activations, but n n is rare, so that clause alone has low recall. Weaker activations come from sequences with n at position 1 or 2 rather than 0, and a small amount comes from the delimiter step when L=4 or 5 and the sequence starts with n. It never fires at t<=2 or t>=8. The predicate gets dev F1 0.66 and mass recall 0.82; most false positives are low-magnitude steps at t=3 or t=6. The input token itself has little effect on magnitude.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=n (+10.84), orig1=n (+5.86), prev_tok=l (+3.44), orig0=v (+2.99), orig2=h (+2.81), t=5 (+2.65). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-12.65), phase=2 (-8.02), t=8 (-8.00), t=7 (-6.46).
